children: U.S. stocks snapped a four-session losing streak as an interruption to the torrid run in oil prices offset a reading of increased consumer inflation.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 509.19 points, or 0.98%, to 52573.29. The S&P 500 added 65.28 points, or 0.86%, to 7656.98 and the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite rose 251.31 points, or 0.96%, to 26333.04.

Oil futures fell $2.43, or 2.4%, to $100.05 a barrel in New York, snapping an eight-session winning streak. Crude gained 9.4% for the week, however, as traders prepared for a protracted disruption of Middle East oil flows due to an escalating conflict. Iran-backed Houthi militants seized a strategic island in the Bab al-Mandeb strait and a town along its mainland coast Friday, taking effective control of one of the world's most important shipping chokepoints.
Oil's retreat overshadowed a firming of August consumer prices. The Consumer Price Index rose 3.4% from a year earlier, buoyed by rising fuel prices.

The yield on the policy-sensitive two-year Treasury rose 0.095 percentage point to  4.642%. The yield on the 10-year Treasury rose 0.031 percentage point to 4.974%, the  highest close since October 2023. The yield on the 30-year bond fell 0.007 percentage point to 5.354% but rose sharply for the week. The 30-year yield has now gained for eight weeks out of the last 11.

One brokerage said the inflation data and recent spikes in Treasury yields would force Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh's hand. "If the Fed were to refrain from hiking after today's data, it would risk a significant selloff at the long end," said strategists at brokerage Bank of America Global Research, in a note to clients, warning of potential disruptions in long-term bonds.
